import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«246»

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1110

*Reference:* [Erdős Problem 1110](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110)
-/

namespace Erdos1110

/--
$n$ is representable with respect to $p$ and $q$ if it is the sum of a finite
divisibility antichain of terms of the form $p^kq^l$.
-/
def Representable (p q n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ s : Finset ℕ,
    (s : Set ℕ) ⊆ Erdos246.Gamma p q ∧
    IsAntichain (· ∣ ·) (s : Set ℕ) ∧
    s.sum id = n

/--
Let $p>q\geq 2$ be two coprime integers. We call $n$ representable if it is the sum of
integers of the form $p^kq^l$, none of which divide each other.

If $\{p,q\}\neq \{2,3\}$ then what can be said about the density of non-representable
numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1110 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (p q : ℕ), q < p → 2 ≤ q →
      Nat.Coprime p q → ¬(p = 3 ∧ q = 2) →
      Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | Nat.Coprime n (p * q) ∧ ¬Representable p q n} := by
  sorry

end Erdos1110

findings.description: The coprimality condition is attached to the wrong objects. Line 49 asks for infinitely many non-representable n individually satisfying gcd(n, p*q) = 1. The source asks for infinitely many coprime nonrepresentables: an infinite mutually coprime family of non-representable integers. Coprimality with the fixed product p*q does not express coprimality between different nonrepresentables, and the Lean statement contains no pairwise condition or existential family enforcing it.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős and Lewin, “d-complete sequences of integers,” Math. Comp. 65 (1996), p. 840, ask: “If p and q are coprime and not 2 and 3 ... what can be said about the density of the nonrepresentable numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime nonrepresentables?” This asks for coprimality among the nonrepresentables, not merely coprimality to pq. The question is repeated on https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110 and in the introduction to Yu–Chen (2022); their Corollary 1.2 uses the same family formulation.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the existing base hypotheses and replace the conclusion with `∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ ∀ n ∈ A, ¬Representable p q n`. This replacement was type-checked in Lean. One may additionally require each member of A to be coprime to p*q: an infinite pairwise coprime family can lose only finitely many members upon excluding the prime factors of p*q. That additional condition cannot replace pairwise coprimality.

sources_consulted: https://web.archive.org/web/20260911000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110 — archived problem page, including remarks and open status

P. Erdős and M. Lewin, “d-complete sequences of integers,” Mathematics of Computation 65 (1996), 837–840; full paper read at https://web.archive.org/web/20100101000000id_/http://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/1996-65-214/S0025-5718-96-00707-7/S0025-5718-96-00707-7.pdf

https://www.impan.pl/get/doi/10.4064/aa220818-20-1 — abstract of Chen–Yu, “On d-complete sequences of integers, II” (2023)
https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1142/S1793042123500732 — abstract of Yu–Chen, “On the d-representation of integers” (2023)
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — publication bibliography consulted while locating the primary paper
review.notes: Both declarations were reviewed. Representable correctly expresses finite sums of nonnegative powers with pairwise nondivisibility. In /workspace/review/computation.lean, I proved its equivalence to a bounded exhaustive search for p,q ≥ 2 and checked small instances. I also proved that allowing n = 0 does not change the non-representable set, and checked the exceptional-pair encoding. The answer slot and quantifier scope are correct. The theorem covers the infinitude subquestion, not the separate density question; that partial coverage is not counted as a defect. Direct website access was blocked, so mathematical sources were read through archives; the current community database also records the general problem as open. The target file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed version.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported issue changes which objects must be coprime, but does not provide a short proof or disproof of the exact universal infinitude statement. Two non-representable numbers individually coprime to pq but sharing a factor would not refute the existence of an infinite pairwise-coprime subfamily, so the previous finite examples are not an adequate demonstration.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created, and no compile was attempted. The earlier boundary computations do not prove or refute the declaration as stated.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported mismatch does not admit a short, honest demonstration under these rules. Proving or refuting the full infinitude assertion would require substantive mathematics; a finite coprimality example would not settle it.

submission.summary: Replaced coprimality with the fixed product p*q by an existential infinite set of pairwise coprime non-representable numbers. Clarified “pairwise” in the docstring while preserving the base hypotheses, definitions, references, and attributes. The requested compilation succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
